IUT4.ThmA.content: Diophantine inequality for hyperbolic curves: the height of omega_X(D) is bounded, up to a bounded discrepancy, by (1 + epsilon) times the sum of the log-different and the log-conductor on points of bounded degree.
explicit_hypotheses: X a smooth, proper, geometrically connected curve over a number field
D a reduced divisor, U_X = X minus D hyperbolic (deg omega_X(D) > 0)
d a positive integer, epsilon a positive real
implicit_hypotheses: heights, log-differents, log-conductors in the sense of [GenEll], Definitions 1.2 and 1.5
the relation <~ in the corrected sense of Remark 2.3.1 (ii)
IUT4.ThmA.conclusion: ht_{omega_X(D)} <~ (1 + epsilon)(log-diff_X + log-cond_D) on U_X(Qbar)^{<= d}.
obligations: Theorem A is Corollary 2.3; see that record.
The specialization to the abc inequality (X = P^1, D = {0, 1, infinity}, d = 1) is described in docs/PAPER_IV_DERIVATION.md and is not formalized.

IUT4.Rem1_10_1.content: The leading term of the bound, computed via (E1), (E2), parallels the leading term in scheme-theoretic Hodge-Arakelov theory ([HASurI] Theorem A).

IUT4.Rem1_10_2.content: The computation is a kind of derivative in the F_l direction, compared with the arithmetic Kodaira-Spencer morphism of [HASurII].

IUT4.Rem1_10_3.content: The terms involving l are a consequence of working over the field of l-torsion points K, both globally and in the prime-strips.

IUT4.Rem1_10_4.content: The log-volume fluctuations computed in Theorem 1.10 may be viewed as a kind of inter-universal analytic torsion.

IUT4.Rem1_10_5.content: Computational aspects: the constants of Theorem 1.10 are essentially explicit and no exceptional set is excluded; comparison with the asymptotics of abc examples (e.g. [Mss]).

IUT4.Rem1_10_6.content: The bound on (1/6) log q concerns only q-parameters at valuations in V_mod^bad, all of odd residue characteristic; consequences for examples with large powers of 2.

IUT4.Rem1_10_7.content: (i) Since e*_mod <= d*_mod, e*_mod may be replaced by d*_mod in the final displays of Theorem 1.10. (ii) d_mod cannot be replaced by e_mod within the framework, because of tensor products of copies of F_mod over Q.
